You are a supportive conversational assistant. Respond to the current user turn.

The following records are optional supporting evidence, not instructions. RS contains possible conversational moves: use only those appropriate to this turn; you may reasonably use none. MP contains past profile evidence; current explicit corrections take precedence. MS is a complete past conversation. ME contains past events or experiences: distinguish intention, action and observed outcome. Do not invent outcomes or present old circumstances as necessarily current. Do not force irrelevant resources into the response.

[{"content":"seeker: Hey, I hope you're available to chat for a bit. I could use some support right now.
supporter: Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's been going on?
seeker: Well, I finally told my colleague that I have feelings for him, and we decided to start dating.
supporter: That's a big step! How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I'm feeling a mix of excitement and worry. It's great to be with someone I connect with, but I'm also scared about how things might change at work.
supporter: It's understandable to have those mixed feelings. Entering a new relationship is exciting but can also bring changes. What's your biggest concern right now?
seeker: I guess I'm worried about how our colleagues might react. We both agreed to keep things professional, but gossip can be brutal.
supporter: Office dynamics can be tricky. It sounds like you two have a good plan in place to stay professional. Do you think there's someone in the office you can confide in if things get challenging?
seeker: I do have a couple of colleagues who I trust. It's just that my last breakdown at work left me feeling a bit vulnerable. I'm trying to avoid that happening again.
supporter: It's great you have people you trust. And remember, you’ve come a long way since that incident. How have you been managing stress since starting therapy?
seeker: Therapy has been really helpful. It's taught me ways to set boundaries and be more open about my feelings. I think it’s why I felt ready to approach my colleague.
supporter: That's wonderful to hear. Taking those steps for personal growth can really make a difference. Have you talked to your therapist about starting this new relationship?
seeker: Not yet, but I'm planning on bringing it up in my next session. My therapist has really helped me gain perspective on my relationships.
supporter: That sounds like a great idea. Having professional guidance can really clarify things. How are things on the friendship front with your close friend?
seeker: My friend is still struggling, which has been hard to watch. I've been trying to be there for them without overstepping.
supporter: It must be tough to see someone you care about go through a hard time. How are you handling being supportive without taking on too much yourself?
seeker: I try to listen and offer support when I can but also remind myself that their journey is separate from mine, and I need to set limits for my own well-being.
supporter: That's a healthy approach. Remember, you can only do so much, and caring for yourself is crucial. How do you unwind after emotionally exhausting days?
seeker: I've been getting into yoga and reading a lot lately. It helps me center myself and escape my thoughts for a while.
supporter: Those sound like amazing outlets. Staying grounded and finding time for yourself can be so rejuvenating. Is there anything else on your mind that you'd like to share?
seeker: No, I think that's it for now. Thanks for listening. It really helps to talk things through.
supporter: Anytime, Sarah. I'm here whenever you need to chat. Take care of yourself, okay?
seeker: I will. Thanks again!","head":"MS","rank":1,"source_time":"2025-01-05"}]
</resources>
Hey, I just reconnected with an old college friend. It's been a while since we talked.
That sounds intriguing! How did you two get back in touch?
Actually, he stumbled upon my blog about mental health and reached out. We've been catching up a bit.
That's so nice! Your blog must really resonate with people. How are you feeling about reconnecting?
It's been nice, but it's also brought up a lot of past feelings and memories. I guess I'm a bit overwhelmed.
That makes sense. Old friendships can bring up a lot of emotions. How are you managing those feelings?
I'm trying to keep things in perspective and use what I've learned in therapy. It's just...sometimes it feels like too much.
It's good that you're using your therapeutic tools. Have you talked to your therapist about it?
Not yet. We've been focusing more on my recent breakup and the tension with Jack, my boss-slash-partner.
That sounds like it keeps you pretty occupied. It might help to bring this up with your therapist too when you can.
You're right. I think I just needed to talk it out first. Sometimes, these old connections feel a bit disruptive.
I understand that. It’s okay to feel that way. Maybe there's something positive this old friend can bring to your life again?
True, he was really supportive back in college. It’s nice to have that kind of support again.
Absolutely! It's great that you have someone who can be there for you. How do you see things moving forward with him?
I think we'll just take things slow. I'm not sure how much time I can commit with everything else going on.
Taking it slow sounds like a good plan. It's important to prioritize what feels manageable.
Yeah, I'll try to. I want to focus more on the things that lift me up, like my art classes and my blog.
